workflow: A registration operation receives a callable and its arguments.
It allocates a temporary owned container for the arguments and incorporates that container into a stored callback record.
The operation succeeds but omits releasing the temporary container after transferring its contents into the record.
Repeated registrations retain each temporary container, so shutdown leak detection reports persistent memory growth.
summary: Successful operation omits cleanup of temporary owned state
decision_reason: The failure mechanism materially matches the existing cluster: a successful operation creates temporary owned heap state, neglects its release, and leaks it across repeated operations.
